items.topic: Study link click data flowing through

items.statement: Strah still needs to finish survey completion, and some work remains on Kobi's side.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: ... But then STR still needs to finish survey completion. Um, and a little bit of work on Kobe's Zen, too. ...

items.statement: WagerTech leans toward owning player ID, deduplication and cleaning, and always passing one player ID from the CMS, but said it still needs to resolve this internally.

items.statement: Emily will book a separate session to discuss the player ID topic.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: No, no. I was just wondering if we like hang back and talk some about the player ID stuff, but maybe later. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, we'll book we'll book something.

items.statement: Kobi asked whether the payout code field is needed for Phase 1, since its automation was not fully defined. Emily said the PRD requires support for payout structure, payment status flow and reporting, but not executing payments in Salesforce.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... So, is this something that's necessary for phase one or do we leave it out for now ... / Emily Vandenberg: ... we're not looking to like execute payment through Salesforce, but we need to be able to push through as like a status or like flow the payments cycle. ...

items.topic: Payout code deferred to payouts object
items.statement: Joyce preferred to handle all payout-related work in the later payouts phase (after redeposits). Kobi agreed: no payout code field or tracking in Salesforce for now; revisit when implementing the payouts object; the bigger payout code generation conversation is tabled.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I would rather treat payouts as like you know how we're moving to redeposits and then we're going to move to payouts / Joyce Kiddell: ... It's like what if we can handle all of just the payout related work at that stage I think that makes more more sense ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. I I'm I'm good with that. So like we don't necessarily need a field or anything to keep track of it on the Salesforce side for now and then we revisit it as part of implementing the payouts / Kobi Kunasekaran: and we'll table the bigger conversation around actual payout code generation for later. That works for me.

items.topic: Paid-signup data gap at payouts launch
items.statement: Emily raised that without some record of which signups were paid, signups would sit open and there would be a gap in the data set when payouts launch.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: ... do we want to like even be able to like kind of upload what has been paid so that we like once we launch we kind of have record um of those signups in Salesforce ... / Emily Vandenberg: If not, they will just kind of sit there open and when we do launch payout, we'll have a bit of a of a gap in our data set.

items.statement: Lina suggested a 'payment sent' checkbox on the signup record. Joyce agreed as a quick solution, and Kobi confirmed Jumpr will add it to the ops view for signup records.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: The only thing I would think to add would be a potential field on the signup record to say like payment sent ... / Joyce Kiddell: I think if the checkbox is like quick and dirty like that totally makes sense just to like close the loop for the rep who's testing. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: like we'll we can add that checkbox. It's pretty straightforward. Um, we'll add it to the ops view um for signup records for payment sent.

items.statement: Joyce said a bigger solutioning meeting is needed on how payouts are handled (batching, payout types and how they merge into the funnel). No owner or date was set.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... and then we definitely just need to have like I think a bigger solutioning meeting around like how we're handling the payout. ... / Joyce Kiddell: ... So, it just requires more discussion in my

items.statement: Lina said redeposit payouts would be a similar 'payment sent' checkbox situation; today WagerTech uses one sheet for signup bank transfers and another for referral payments.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: ... And then rate deposits are kind of a different thing when it comes to payouts ... / Lina Ceniccola: like that would be another kind of checkbox situation where it's just like payment sent payment sent payment sent. So, cuz right now we have a sheet to manage bank transfers for every sign up that's sent out and then we have another sheet to trans to manage the referral payments for all those payments sent out.

items.statement: Kobi asked whether the ops cost calculation formula should be in Phase 1 or a later phase, since information is missing. Emily said it had been discussed for Phase 1. No phase decision was made.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Is this something that we want to approach similar to PR code uh at a later phase or is this something that we want to add in as part of phase one? / Emily Vandenberg: We had talked about adding it to phase one in one of our sessions, but I just didn't know what you were missing for the calculations and the formulas.

items.topic: Kobi to specify ops cost needs
items.statement: Kobi will review his notes and come back with what is available and what the ops cost fields/formula could look like; Emily will provide whatever is needed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, let me go back on my notes and get back to you with like the specifics of like what we have right now and what this could look like with the information that we / Emily Vandenberg: whatever you need like we'll kind of get it over to / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think if I remember correctly, we were just going to add some fields to support this, but yeah, I'll have to go back to my notes and I'll get back to you.

items.statement: Kobi will go through the rest of Emily's feedback/comments and get back to her.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... I'll have to go through the rest of the feedback and I can get back to you on those uh afterwards, Emily. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... And yeah, like I'll review your comments and feedback as well, Emily ...

items.topic: Scope shift to full CMS integration
items.statement: Kobi said the direction has moved from deal rep assignments and logic in Salesforce to all Salesforce data going into the CMS.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: The CMS integration. I mean that's kind of like that's the direction we're going now. / Kobi Kunasekaran: We started with DRF assignments and logic and now we're just talking about um all the Salesforce data going into the CMS.
items.supersedes_hint: Started with deal rep assignments and logic; now all Salesforce data going into the CMS.
items.asr_note: deal wrap EMS / DRF = deal rep / CMS [ASR?]

items.statement: Emily questioned the design doc line that Salesforce pushes a deal and its links to the CMS as options. Joyce said the pivot is still a concept of rep assignment in Salesforce, but giving reps options (possibly multiple links per deal) rather than a strict one-to-one link.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: so published Salesforce pushes a deal and its links to the CMS uh where they become options to choose from. / Emily Vandenberg: I thought we moved to like we're actually like assigning at a rep level into the CMS into / Joyce Kiddell: So, I think what we were kind of pivoting towards is still um having like a concept of rep assignment in Salesforce, but it's more like providing um the reps with options for people to choose from.

items.statement: Per Emily and Lina, a rep typically has one link per deal at a time but can be moved to a different link on the same deal; there will also be rep sharing (multiple reps assigned to one link), managed from Salesforce as master.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: typically like a rep for a deal wouldn't have more than one link, but they like to maintain it like they might get moved around from time to time but it would be managed on Salesforce so it' be like updated in that master like Salesforce and then that would be show available in the CMS then there will be rep sharing so like multiple / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, there's a potential for them to switch to a different link on the same / Lina Ceniccola: deal.

items.statement: Joyce thinks link changes should happen on the CMS side, because only Owen and possibly one other person make these changes and doing it in the current Salesforce state is clunkier.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: And in my mind, I keep thinking like that should happen on the CMS side because like for lack of needing to bring in more people onto the Salesforce view, right? / Joyce Kiddell: But like we're adamant that it's only Owen and potentially like one other person that changes this stuff. So if that's the case, then it just is a bit clunkier / Joyce Kiddell: in my mind in the current Salesforce state.

items.topic: WagerTech to review and confirm design
items.statement: WagerTech (Joyce) will go through where the deal rep / CMS design landed and loop back with confirmation; Emily said it is in WagerTech's court.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Okay, maybe we just like give you the like some time to just like go through where we landed, play, and then like loop back on / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah. Okay. So, I think there Kobe is just like I know you were like looking for kind of feedback. / Emily Vandenberg: It's in our court. We will Joyce will kind of like review confirm. ...

items.statement: Kobi restated the proposed workflow: the deal and its related links are configured in Salesforce, sent as one payload to the CMS (pending WagerTech's API endpoint), rep-to-link assignment is done in the CMS, then pushed back to Salesforce, which creates and maintains the deal rep assignment records.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... they go into Salesforce create the deal record ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: all like pending how you configure your API endpoint. But we would send a payload of the deal configuration and all the links uh to CMS and then in CMS you would uh associate or add the deal rep assignments. So, choose the rep, choose the link from the deal, um, and choose the deal, uh, and do the assignment on the CMS side. And that gets pushed back to Salesforce. And Salesforce will then create and maintain these records based on what we're getting from the CMS.

items.statement: Joyce needs to understand how Owen views the overall rep/link assignments (today in Airtable) before confirming; she asked for a separate discussion and did not confirm in the meeting.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: last week is that we um I guess it would update in table, but I just need to understand I think like how Owen looks at like the overall view and then like makes decisions. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. For like who he's assigned to what. Like I know it's an air table. Um anyway, I I just need to not confirm right now. / Joyce Kiddell: I think I need to have a separate discussion. I'm sorry to keep drawing this

items.statement: Kobi said the two-way CMS integration (API callouts) is a large build that is mostly net new versus the original plan, which covered only study link clicks into Salesforce and deal rep management in the Salesforce UI; some deal rep management is pulled ahead. Waleed confirmed the original was only the incoming API connection and a custom build is needed for Salesforce to talk to the CMS. Emily said WagerTech could not yet confirm whether it is additional or pull-ahead scope.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: is a pretty big build that we're adding uh in addition to like the payouts objects and everything that we had queued up right um we hadn't talked about like a twoe integration like this initially we just scoped out the study link clicks coming into Salesforce. / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... some of it is like we are pulling ahead like the whole concept of like deal rep management but the integration specifically like the API callouts and stuff that is a lot of that is new from what we initially discussed ... / Waleed Alasadi: Yeah, correct. It was just the incoming kind of API connection. / Waleed Alasadi: I really don't know what you call it. So it has to be kind of built specifically um to to talk to your CMS.

items.statement: Emily said WagerTech will get back to Jumpr on the detailed CMS integration scope document.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: that makes sense. Um, okay. Yeah, that let us get back to you on your kind of like detailed scope doc

items.statement: Waleed asked why Owen would manage assignments in the CMS rather than Salesforce. Emily said setup and config are in Salesforce and link on/off activation is in the CMS; Joyce said she shares Waleed's question.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Um, I guess I'm struggling to understand, and I'm sure you have your reasons, but I'm struggling to understand why would Owen log into the CMS to manage a lot of the assignments and the views and not Salesforce itself. / Emily Vandenberg: So the setup and config is like Salesforce. The onoff CMS. / Joyce Kiddell: But like why wouldn't I think I'm kind of aligned with bull where it's like why why wouldn't we just do the onoff in Salesforce too? Like do more people do on off piece than just knowing?

items.statement: Joyce explained the CMS connects to external systems: the links a rep has access to show up on dedicated websites/portals, so assignment cannot be configured in Salesforce in isolation; if a rep is not assigned to a link the signup flow cannot complete.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... Like where I'm getting tripped up is on the CMS side. It's actually tied to external systems ... / Joyce Kiddell: then it's not going to show up in their portal and then like we can't complete the actual like sign up or conversion flow.

items.statement: Kobi suggested that, since WagerTech is rebuilding the CMS, a CMS API endpoint for link assignment and activation could let Salesforce drive assignment, noting it adds scope on both ends. Joyce said this needs an internal WagerTech discussion.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... could we not have an API endpoint to do the link assignment and activation ... / Joyce Kiddell: serves. Uh yeah, I think it's just an internal discussion that we need to have in terms of like I'm still having this like identity crisis of like what is the purpose of CMS versus Salesforce. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I mean that does add a lot of scope on both ends, right? ...

items.statement: Kobi said WagerTech will review the document, and any further CMS-side changes must be factored into the design before Jumpr makes changes.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, no. So, I think right now where I'm at is um you'll review the document and then any any further changes that you're making on the CMS side, um, let's make sure to factor those in into the design before we make any changes.

items.statement: Kobi offered to start building the link object and fields (link code, link URL) now to work in parallel. Emily suggested WagerTech loop back first and decide based on how much changes.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... I can start building out the I think I mentioned this in the talk already but the whole uh the link object and everything we can start building that uh right now ... / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, I think let's maybe just have kind of like we'll loop back and then we can / Emily Vandenberg: decide from there. See how much it changes.

items.statement: Emily said the August 15 Phase 1 date will not be met due to new scope on both sides and WagerTech technology delays; Kobi later confirmed alignment that mid-August will not be hit.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: ... we know we're not we're not hitting August 15th. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I think like as long as we're aligned that like we're not hitting the mid August, which it sounds like we're not going to. ...

items.topic: WagerTech clearer rollout plan next week
items.statement: Emily said WagerTech committed to being clearer next week on timeline and rollout plan.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: ... we kind of committed to like next week being a bit clearer on our end on like timeline on the on the kind of rollout plan. ...

items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: ... we need to like land a few things on the agency site CMS this week as well ... / Emily Vandenberg: the CMS and the websites aren't like even live yet to be able to plug into the API data right for us to even kind of start. So that's like the recognition of we we're causing some delay as well. Once we kind of like get that a bit more firmed up on our end this week, I think we can like better understand what that broader,

items.statement: Waleed suggested getting reps into Salesforce early (at least with the signup process) and adding features every two to three weeks, rather than postponing go-live; Jumpr is biased toward getting WagerTech live.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: ... So I'm wondering if there's a world where like we are able to get the users your your like sales reps into Salesforce maybe using the signup process at least ... / Waleed Alasadi: it's obvious uh we're biased towards getting you live because I just like I'm just going to put it out there

items.statement: Waleed asked WagerTech to consider what is sufficient for Phase 1 go-live; Emily said WagerTech will take it away and have a more meaningful discussion next week.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: ... So, it's just important to consider what you think is sufficient for phase one now that you've seen kind of what we have. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, let us take it away. I think like and all kind of points considering next week we can have a more meaningful kind of discussion around it. Okay.

items.statement: Joyce asked if the signup flow can be tested next week without deal assignment. Waleed said Jumpr is ready; Kobi said the signup process (SLC ingestion, signup records, signup workflows, log buttons) can be ready if the CMS and Salesforce have the same operator and partner lists; the CMS generates player IDs.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Like are we able to start testing just like the sign up flow next week without / Joyce Kiddell: deal assignment? / Waleed Alasadi: We're We're ready. / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... So in a nutshell like yes we can be ready from the sign up process um assuming we have uh like both CMS and Salesforce have the same operator and partner list um for players um CMS is generating the ID so I think that's okay ...

items.statement: From the call with Strah: Salesforce would send operator and partner IDs to the CMS so the CMS has external IDs to send back. In the interim, the same data and IDs could be uploaded to both systems until the Salesforce-to-CMS connection exists.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... we talked about having Salesforce send the operator and partner IDs to CMS as well, so that you have the external IDs to send back into Salesforce. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... or if we just make sure both systems have the same data and ids um uploaded to both systems which we could do in the time being until we have the connection back from like connection from Salesforce to CMS. ...

items.statement: Without the API-managed deal rep assignment, signups will not link to deals unless an interim manual deal rep assignment process is agreed; otherwise the data will be incomplete.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... what we won't necessarily have is those signups linking back to deals unless we decide on an interim process to create these uh deal rep assignments ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... then we need to come up with a manual way to do it in the interim otherwise it won't be like the data won't be complete

items.statement: Joyce asked about running test clicks through a staging/sandbox agency site; Emily said WagerTech can spin one up (it had not gone that way before). Joyce also suggested extending existing website testers' testing to see if it hits Salesforce.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. So, we could potentially even just extend their testing like to see if it's like hitting in / Joyce Kiddell: ... do we have like I thought we had a test version of one of the agency sites it like a sandbox. / Emily Vandenberg: I think we can spin one up. We didn't end up going that

items.statement: Joyce wants actual users giving UX feedback on the signup flow soon, even with non-real data; Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... if we're able to just like start having someone provide us with actual like feedback on like the user experience. / Joyce Kiddell: let's test it let's get some people in there like even if it's not real data I just want someone getting their hands on like the actual UI that isn't us a / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, agreed.

items.statement: Kobi described the GCP/Drive proof-of-concept design: proofs are decoupled from storage architecture (today reps paste links into three proof link fields); the integration adds upload buttons on the signup record that save files to Google Drive, tag them (for example as signup proof), and write the link back into Salesforce, plus other file uploads.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... in the signup records we have these three link fields um where right now you can paste in the links and this will uh consider the proof as being uploaded. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... we would essentially have a button that lets you uh upload the files from your computer and then um that will pop to Google Drive, save the file there, get the link back and paste it into uh into Salesforce. ...

items.statement: Joyce requires that each rep only has access to and visibility of their own proofs (a walled garden per rep, like their Salesforce records), with a separate provision for an operations role to see everything.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: you should only have access and visibility over your own proofs, right? In the same way that in Salesforce, you only have visibility over your own signups and rate deposits and stuff like that, right? So, it's like a walled garden per rep. / Joyce Kiddell: the number one thing for me is making sure that there's no overlapping like visibility, right, between the reps and we need to have like a separate provision for uh like operations / Joyce Kiddell: rule to be able to see everything, right? ...

items.statement: Kobi said Jumpr does no development on the Google side; folder privacy and sharing are configured by WagerTech when setting up Drive and providing a credential. Joyce accepted, as long as Jumpr writes to the correct folders. Folder mapping logic still needs to be worked out.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... we're not doing any uh any development on the Google Cloud side of things for this, right? ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: we're not touching any of those. That's all configured for us as part of like setting up the Google Drive and providing us a credential. / Joyce Kiddell: As long as you're writing to the correct folders, then that would be / Joyce Kiddell: fine. / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... We need to hash out that logic so that we know on our end when somebody's uploading the proof where to upload.

items.statement: Joyce sketched a possible folder hierarchy: rep, then player name, then operator or signup, then date.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: and the structure would be like the structure would be like kind of rep. / Joyce Kiddell: I'm just like doodling rep and then under that would be like player / Joyce Kiddell: name and then like hypothetically player name and then um like operator or like sign up whatever and then date. So you're basically looking like for what does that hierarchy look like from us? Okay.

items.statement: Waleed suggested using Google Workspace AI to move and share uploaded files instead of hardcoding folder logic. Joyce said it would need reps on WagerTech's Workspace, and not all reps have email addresses, so it is not practical right now.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: ... if like Kobe and team are able to structure the files or give you tags within the file and you kind of put in the logic to have it moved and like shared however you want within the AI. ... / Joyce Kiddell: because they currently do not have not all of them have like email addresses associated with / Joyce Kiddell: I just don't know that it's practical for us right

items.statement: Kobi suggested tabling GCP and focusing on deal, deal rep assignment and CMS API work first. Joyce suggested Jumpr focus on GCP while WagerTech confirms the deal side. Kobi will check resourcing before deciding the sequence.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... If this is not urgent, I would table this for later and focus on deal and deal rep assignment and CMS API work first. / Joyce Kiddell: ... I would probably focus your efforts on the GCP while we're like 100% confirming stuff, I guess, entirely on the deal side of things. ...

items.statement: Kobi will check Jumpr resourcing and report back on whether GCP work can start alongside CMS integration configuration.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay, let me check our our resourcing on our side too. ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... But if the CMS integration isn't going to be ready for a couple weeks anyways, then uh and we're able to uh staff it on our end to work on the GCP, uh I can try to get that going while I'm working on the configuration parts. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I can get back to you. I'll let you know. ...

items.statement: Kobi said this week Jumpr has a lot of behind-the-scenes automation updates for SLC clicks to make.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh we have a lot of behind the scenes um automations to update um the SLC click uh updates that we need to make. So there's actually quite a bit of work to do um to get the one ready to go.

items.topic: WagerTech settle deal side by week-end
items.statement: Joyce said WagerTech is going to have the deal side figured out by the end of the week.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... Because if you were waiting on us for like the deal stuff ... / Joyce Kiddell: like we're going to have this figured out by the end of the week ...

items.statement: Kobi wants to build and prove file send and API calls first, then iterate on folder locations and structure. Joyce said Jumpr is not blocked and can proceed; Emily said Kobi is good if the design does not deviate from what was discussed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... like for the purpose of the PC, I want to make sure that we're able to send the files, uh, build out the API calls and everything, get those working, and then we can, uh, talk through the actual like locations, folder structure, and everything, um, as an iterative process. / Joyce Kiddell: You're not you're not blocked on that piece. / Joyce Kiddell: Like you can just do this. / Emily Vandenberg: like if everything else is like pretty like standard to what we've talked about, nothing like deviates from I think like what we've been talking around here, Kobe, then I think you're good.

items.statement: Joyce asked whether storage compression is scoped. Kobi said there is no compression in the design; compression or encryption of files is on the Google Drive side, which Joyce accepted as a WagerTech internal item (a discussion point with Strah).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... is that scoped anywhere in here? / Kobi Kunasekaran: We're not doing any compression ... / Joyce Kiddell: like files themselves that would be something that we have to look at internally probably right. / Kobi Kunasekaran: yeah like that's all on the Google Drive / Joyce Kiddell: ... So maybe um that's just a quick discussion point with Straw ...

items.statement: Kobi noted reps only see links on signup records they own and need a Google account to open them; whether explicit link restrictions requiring login with the right account are needed is to be discussed later.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So I don't know if that like that kind of restriction is good enough or if you need explicit restrictions on the links so that you have to be logged in with the right account. We can talk about that later. Um but for now

items.statement: Joyce wants to talk through the upload interface when the work reaches that stage; Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. And I the one thing I will care about is like the upload interface. So talking through kind of when what that looks like when we get to that / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay.

So, Emily, like I I can coordinate with you to get that figured out once you're ready to start. / Kobi Kunasekaran: to your like it's Google Drive so to your / Joyce Kiddell: So Emily, that's an Alex thing.

items.statement: Kobi clarified the proposal uses Google Drive through a service account (similar to Dropbox), not the Google Cloud Platform itself, so users can find and process proofs without cloud platform access.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... ultimately what we're using is not the actual like cloud platform itself, it's still Google Drive ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... So um what we're proposing here it's it's Google Drive essentially through a service account where we're s storing everything very similar to uh Dropbox. ...

items.topic: Add Drive permission level to doc

items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, and in your doc, do you have the level of permission you need? / Kobi Kunasekaran: It should. If not, I'll get that for you added in.

items.statement: Joyce introduced a fraud tool another vendor is building for the welcome email stage: players forward the operator welcome email to a single inbox per agency domain with rep aliases; checks run, results are written to a Google Sheet, the rep is notified via WhatsApp, and the email is forwarded to the rep's real inbox. This is WagerTech's Phase 1 of the tool.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... So, we have another vendor who's building a um a fraud tool for us specific to the welcome email stage. ... / Joyce Kiddell: ... Once we have the results, it's going to um write that to a Google sheet plus also send a notification to the rep ...

items.statement: In the fraud tool's Phase 2, results would move from the Google Sheet onto individual player records, likely via API; WagerTech will own the code and will probably build an endpoint.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... Phase two will be actually um pulling out the results from the Google Sheets obviously and storing that against the individual player records. / Joyce Kiddell: So I'm assuming at that point we'll do it via API. Um and they're building it for us. / Joyce Kiddell: So we're going to own all the code like it's being pulled into our GitHub um or uh so we'll just have to build you probably an endpoint for that one as well.

items.statement: The welcome email check applies to affiliate signups and happens after the signup record is created (a click creates the signup record).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Is this like the welcome emails for the like the affiliate signups or for your agency website signup? / Kobi Kunasekaran: The affiliate signups. Okay. Um, / Kobi Kunasekaran: and is this happening uh before the signup record gets created or after? After. Right. Okay. / Joyce Kiddell: ... When there's a click, it's there's no like lead. So, yes, it we will have a signup record ...

items.statement: Once connected via API, receipt of the welcome email notification would move the signup record to In Progress, as an automated trigger discussed previously; endpoint direction to be sorted out later.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: ... the goal would be that um once we have it connected via / Joyce Kiddell: API, um the receipt of that welcome email notification makes it in progress. / Joyce Kiddell: We discussed that as like an automated trigger / Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Whether you send it from your end or we query it from our end,

items.statement: Kobi asked whether the fraud tool API integration is Phase 1 or fast follow; Joyce answered fast follow, treating items as they come in, and prioritizing signup flow testing.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Player ID ownership responsibility Responsibility for player ID, deduplication, and cleaning is assigned to the CMS team to ensure consistent data processing.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Emily Vandenberg: We need to resolve it on our end, but what we kind of lean towards is like we own player ID um and dduping and cleaning and making sure we're always passing one through from the CMS. Excuse me.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary lists this as Aligned/assigned; transcript says WagerTech only leans toward it and still needs to resolve it internally (firmer than transcript).

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Ops cost formula postponed Implementation of the ops cost calculation formula is postponed until additional information regarding requirements is available.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Emily Vandenberg: We had talked about adding it to phase one in one of our sessions, but I just didn't know what you were missing for the calculations and the formulas. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, let me go back on my notes and get back to you with like the specifics of like what we have right now and what this could look like with the information that we
